text.content:
Calling represents a bond between your character and a supernatural entity — a spirit, ancestor, or other manifested power. Most Calling cards channel only a piece of that bond. You stay in play, playing yourself.

Full Manifestation is the Style's fixed Rider: your character steps aside and the form takes their place on the battlefield, using its own Defenses, Resilience, Movement, Senses, Roll Limit and granted Actions and Reactions. You are not gaining a second creature; you disappear, and it stands where you were, as the same character for Initiative, Turn and Reaction-chain purposes.

Forms come in fixed families by Rank: Familiar and Sprite at Rank 0; Beast, Phantom and Golem at Rank 1; Elemental, Ancestor and Fey at Rank 2 (Ranks 3 to 5 name Dragon, Fiend, Celestial, Abomination, Leviathan, Avatar, Outsider, Titan and Primordial, without profiles yet). The rulebook supplies no numeric profiles in this edition; the eight in the Calling Full Manifestations compendium are Campaign-supplied playtest profiles.

Play an eligible Calling Action as normal and pay its printed cost. Then open your sheet's header menu and choose Full Manifestation. Each form in the list shows the Rider's surcharge, which is paid automatically when you enter: extra burned Action dice and extra Mana by the form's Rank.

The Summoner's Greater Manifestation reduces only the burned-die surcharge by 1. The underlying card still costs its full minimum, at least 2 Pool dice. You need the dice available; short Mana warns. You cannot enter while Broken, and you must return before entering another form.

You aren't getting a fresh Turn. The form picks up exactly where you left off: your remaining Action and Reaction Dice are all it has, Movement already spent stays spent, and the response you used in a chain stays used. Your own Wounds, Conditions, Death Track and durations pause underneath — manifesting heals nothing.

Your card options shrink to the form's own granted Actions and Reactions; universal Basics, your learned cards and Species or Equipment Actions are not inherited unless the profile says so. Native cards use the Rank's minimum commitment (the form's sheet enforces it) and the form's printed Roll Limit as their maximum; Mana costs come out of your own Mana. Prepared Actions still expire on schedule.

To leave, click Return (burn 1) on the form's sheet during your Turn: 1 Action die is burned, your token swaps back, and the form's Conditions and Temporary Wounds end. The form otherwise stays until it collapses, the Encounter ends (New Encounter returns you for free), or an effect ends it.

All of your forms share one five-space Manifestation Wound track, shown as pips in the Calling row of your Combat tab. When you enter a form, its sheet shows that track as it stands; Wounds it takes fill the shared track, and they stay filled when you return and when you enter another form later. Manifestation Wounds cause no Wound Cards for you. The active form uses its own Resilience and any Temporary Wounds it gains; your paused Wounds never transfer.

Apply Damage on the form's sheet resolves each component in order. Your accumulated ordinary Damage carries into the form and back, so switching bodies never shrugs off a hit that already landed.

Collapse and Broken

When a component fills the fifth space, the form collapses at once. The rest of that component's Wounds are discarded, your token returns, and you directly suffer 1 Spiritual Core Wound that bypasses Resilience, Resistance and Temporary Wounds (a full Core track advances the Death Track instead). Any later components of that hit are posted to chat for the GM to recheck against you by hand. The shared track stays full and you are Broken: no Full Manifestation, though ordinary Calling cards still work. Each Recovery removes 1 Manifestation Wound, and removing one from a full track ends Broken. The pips on your sheet can also be adjusted by hand.

Every profile shares the caller's five-space Manifestation Wound track, so no profile has a Wound capacity of its own. A profile marked Living is a valid target for a living-only effect; one marked Nonliving is not — but it still feels pain, can be restrained, and is affected by mental attacks, magic, and ordinary Conditions. Being a Phantom doesn't make you incorporeal.

Open any profile from the Calling Full Manifestations compendium to read its stat block and maneuvers. These are Campaign-supplied playtest profiles; the GM may add a Roll Limit in the header.

The first time a character fully manifests a given subtype, the system creates that character's own persistent copy of the profile and gives the controlling player Owner permission on it — you don't need to drag anything from the compendium. Later manifestations of the same subtype reuse that copy.

Entering, returning and collapse are one click each: the entry surcharge is deducted, the token swaps, and the shared Manifestation Wound track is copied in and written back. Collapse applies the caller's direct Spiritual Core Wound and its Wound Card and marks the caller Broken. What stays by hand: rechecking any later Damage components of a collapsing hit against the returned caller (posted to chat), and judging whether the form fits its space when it appears or returns.

If a track was filled by hand-toggled pips rather than Apply Damage, the form's header menu offers Collapse (track full) to run the same collapse.
